description: Set several places at once, like jsonx_set for each item, in the order given (for plain data use json_multi_set). Each item: {"path": FILE#/POINTER} plus exactly one of "value" (any JSON, stored as given) / "text" (parsed as JSON) / "from" (copied from FILE#/POINTER). The options apply to every item: resolve, follow, check, parents (as in jsonx_set). One line per item: PATH, a TAB, then "ok ..." or "[error] CODE reason". Items are independent and nothing is undone; if any failed the last line is "jsonx_multi_set: error: PlacesFailed ...". Example: {"items": [{"path": "fsm.json#/states/act/exec", "from": "lib.json#/exec"}, {"path": "fsm.json#/max", "value": 30}], "follow": true}.

items.description: the changes, each {"path": "FILE#/POINTER"} plus exactly one of "value", "text", "from"; at least one; done in this order

parents.description: true = create missing objects along the way for every item (like mkdir -p)

resolve.description: true = for every item, resolve $ref/$env inside the value before storing; false = store them as written

follow.description: true = for every item, go through $ref on the way and change the file it points to; false = a $ref/$env on the way is an error (FollowMissing)

check.description: true = refuse each change that adds problems to the aos configuration
